request.text: Sorting by date on the reports table throws a client error when some rows have a null date.

open_questions.default: Assume the comparator is defined and exported (or at least testable) from useDocumentReportsData.ts, since its docstring identifies it as the likely location of sorting logic.
open_questions.q: Is the date sort comparator defined inline inside useDocumentReportsData.ts, or is it passed in from/shared with DocumentReportsPage.tsx (e.g. as a column definition for a table library)?

tasks.description: In src/features/analytics/documents/components/hooks/useDocumentReportsData.ts, locate the sort comparator used for date columns and update it to handle null/undefined values explicitly: treat missing dates as always sorting after valid dates in both ascending and descending order, and avoid calling .getTime() or arithmetic directly on a possibly-null value.
tasks.done_criteria: Calling the date comparator with a mix of null, undefined, and valid Date values returns a sorted array without throwing, and rows with null dates are consistently placed last
tasks.title: Guard date comparator against null values

tasks.description: Add src/features/analytics/documents/components/hooks/useDocumentReportsData.test.ts covering the date comparator/sort function with cases: all valid dates, some null, some undefined, and all null, for both ascending and descending order. Assert no exception is thrown and the resulting order places null/undefined consistently.
tasks.done_criteria: New test suite passes against the fixed comparator and fails (throws) against the pre-fix implementation
tasks.title: Unit test null-safe date sorting

assumptions.text: The sort comparator for date columns lives inside useDocumentReportsData.ts (per its tier-2 docstring 'sorting logic likely invoked here') and is a plain JS function comparing two row values, not a third-party grid library's built-in sorter.
The fix should treat null/undefined dates as sorting after all valid dates in both asc and desc order (a common convention), rather than adding a separate UI toggle for null placement.

A new test file useDocumentReportsData.test.ts does not yet exist in the pack and needs to be created alongside the hook, following the repo's convention of colocating hook tests, to unit-test the comparator in isolation.

criteria.given: the document reports table is rendered with rows where some date field values are null and others are valid Date/ISO values
criteria.then: the sort completes without throwing a client error and returns an array of the same length with rows containing null dates placed consistently (e.g. always last) relative to rows with valid dates
criteria.when: the user triggers a sort on that date column (ascending or descending)

criteria.given: a mixed array of report rows with null, undefined, and valid date values for the sorted field
criteria.then: it returns a stable, error-free ordering with no thrown exception and no NaN comparisons
criteria.when: the sort comparator function used by useDocumentReportsData is called directly with these rows

non_goals: Will not modify prisma/schema.prisma because the nullable date columns are intentional business fields, not a schema defect
Will not modify src/features/analytics/documents/queries/document-reports.ts because the null dates originate from legitimate missing data upstream, not from the query construction
Will not modify src/features/analytics/documents/export-service.ts because the reported error is a client-side sorting crash in the table UI, not the export flow
spec.problem_statement: The reports table in src/features/analytics/documents/components/DocumentReportsPage.tsx throws a client-side error when sorting by a date column that contains null values (e.g. DocumentRevision.revisionDate, validTill, or publishedOn are optional per prisma/schema.prisma). The sort logic in useDocumentReportsData.ts likely calls a date comparison (e.g. .getTime() or direct comparison) without guarding for null/undefined, causing a runtime TypeError. Done means sorting any date column completes without throwing, with null dates consistently ordered (placed last regardless of sort direction).
